the leukocyte migration test was useful for in vitro study on cell‐mediated immunity in patients with malignancies.
autogenous leukocyte migration was inhibited in vitro in the presence of fresh, frozen and thawed tumor cells, or extracts of tumor cells, in patients with localized tumors.
the L.M.T. is a useful tool for the in vitro study of the host's immune reaction to the autogenous tumor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cell‐mediated immunity in patients with various human malignancies, using the L.M.T.
the in vitro study of the cellmediated immunity of the autogenous peripheral blood cells in human malignancies by the L.M.T.
the in vitro demonstration of the presence of a cell‐mediated immune response in human malignancies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the leukocyte migration test is a useful tool to evaluate cellmediated immunity against tumors in humans.
the leukocyte migration test is a useful method in the study of cellmediation immunity, and it is a valuable tool for the evaluation of the immunologic status of the host.
the leukocyte migration test can be utilized as a tool for studying cell‐mediated immunity in man.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the leukocyte migration test is a simple, reproducible, and reliable method for the study of cell‐mediated immunity in man, and it may be useful in the evaluation and prognosis of human malignancies.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the leukocyte migration test can be utilized as a simple, sensitive, and reliable test for the study of cell‐mediated immunity in humans.
the L.M.T. is a simple and sensitive in vitro method for studying cell‐mediated immunity in man.
the L.M.T. can be utilized to study the state of cellmediated immune response in human malignancies and to predict whether a given tumor will be resectable or metastasize.
